questions.question: What physical cause does the author propose for the anomalous gyromagnetic ratio, in contrast to the usual compositeness explanation?

options.A: A finite particle size plus spin–Lorentz-force interaction in curved spacetime
options.B: A purely electromagnetic radiative correction to a point particle
options.C: A strong interaction correction that applies only to quarks
options.D: A nonzero magnetic charge induced by the curved metric

questions.rationale: The proposal attributes the anomaly to finite spatial extent and curvature, not necessarily substructure.
questions.evidence_quote: because particles do have a finite size and that spacetime is curved

questions.question: What gyromagnetic ratios does the introduction cite for the proton and neutron as examples where the bare Dirac prediction fails?
questions.rationale: These measured values are contrasted with the Dirac value g=2.
questions.evidence_quote: The Proton was found to have a gyromagnetic ratio gp = 5.58

questions.question: How does the author define the curved-spacetime energy shift term Pc in the proposed dispersion relation?

options.A: Pc=Σᵢ|pᵢ|c, taken strictly positive under the assumed orientation of time relative to spatial axes
options.B: Pc=Σᵢpᵢ²c², the invariant spatial momentum norm
options.C: Pc=−Σᵢ|pᵢ|c, fixed by the negative-energy branch

questions.rationale: The article introduces Pc as the sum of absolute momentum components and makes it positive by assumption.

questions.question: What corrected qualification does the paper's Key Note add to the original claim about positive- and negative-energy solutions?

options.A: Solutions are not exclusively positive or negative; the author says the original statement contained a slit error
options.B: All solutions become exclusively positive once curvature is included
options.C: The corrected version removes all negative-energy solutions in every case
options.D: Only antiparticle solutions remain after the correction

questions.rationale: The opening note explicitly corrects the claim of exclusive positive/negative solutions.
questions.evidence_quote: the present theory results in solutions that are exclussively positive or negative which is not the case

questions.question: For the position-independent wavefunction case, what does the curved equation reduce to?

options.A: The flat-spacetime time-dependent Dirac equation, yielding Φ∝e⁺ⁱᵐᶜᵗ/ℏ and χ∝e⁻ⁱᵐᶜᵗ/ℏ
options.B: A scalar Klein–Gordon equation with only positive-frequency solutions
options.C: A pair of coupled equations with identical time phases
options.D: An equation with no solutions unless momentum is nonzero

questions.rationale: The author first analyzes the spatially constant case and reports the same positive/negative energy phases as flat space.
questions.evidence_quote: which is the same as the flat spacetime Dirac equation

questions.question: What does the author claim is required for the proposed absence of negative-energy solutions in a spatially dependent state?

options.A: Dependence on time and on at least one spatial coordinate
options.C: Dependence on all three spatial coordinates simultaneously
options.D: A vanishing rest mass and zero magnetic field

questions.rationale: The paper says negative solutions disappear when the wavefunction depends on at least one position coordinate, forcing time and spatial dependence together.
questions.evidence_quote: the wave-function of the particle must always be dependent on both time and at least one of the space coordinates

questions.question: In the paper's nonrelativistic magnetic coupling, what multiplicative factor modifies the usual spin contribution relative to g=2?
questions.rationale: Equation (35) places this factor on the spin operator, with λc the Compton wavelength and Rp the proposed radius.
questions.evidence_quote: for every unit of spin angular momentum

questions.question: How does the author relate the proposed particle radius to its kinematics in deriving the modified spin coupling?

options.A: Using the n=1 Bohr condition gives v=ℏ/(mRp), with Rp also identified as the de Broglie wavelength
options.B: Setting the radius equal to the Compton wavelength makes v=c
options.D: The radius is defined as the inverse magnetic field strength

questions.rationale: The paper adopts the first Bohr orbit condition as a heuristic size model.
questions.evidence_quote: Taking the case n = 1, we have v = ℏ/mRp

options.C: It cannot assign positive mass to antiparticles
options.D: It proves that the muon is stable in the present universe
